title: Riograndense Republic
capsule: The Riograndense Republic was a secessionist state proclaimed by Farroupilha rebels in the province of Rio Grande do Sul on 11 September 1836, declaring independence from the Brazilian Empire after an initial revolt that broke out in 1835. Led by Bento Gonçalves da Silva and, later, the Italian revolutionary Giuseppe Garibaldi (who also fought in Uruguay's Cisplatine War), the republic adopted a federalist constitution influenced by Platine models. Despite some military successes the republic lacked recognition from any foreign power and suffered from blockade and internal division; peace was concluded in the Convention of Ponche Verde on 1 March 1845, reincorporating the province into Brazil with an amnesty and other concessions.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The republic's territorial extent is broadly attested as the province of Rio Grande do Sul, though actual control fluctuated considerably with military fortunes; no precise cartographic surveys were conducted during the conflict.
